# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.
- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — the generic challenge model this feature generalises.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.

2. 3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.

# Intake Brief — Refactor: decompose MainStreet god modules (CG-0MTP6KLQD001TBMH)

## Problem Statement

Nine Main Street modules exceed the 800-line threshold (Engine 2720, Animator 1948, Renderer 1908, TurnController 1821, plus State 1582, Adjacency 1583, Cards 1469, Market 1311, LifecycleManager 1111), each mixing state, rendering, animation, and turn logic. This violates maintainability and the project's god-class threshold, slowing future feature work and increasing regression risk.

## Users

- **Engine/Game maintainers** — need navigable, single-responsibility modules to change rules, animations, or rendering without editing 1900+ line files.
- **Game developers extending Main Street** — need clear per-concern helpers to reuse or test in isolation (e.g., income animation vs. market validation).

### User Stories

- As a maintainer, I want MainStreetEngine split so turn phases, action dispatch, and scoring are in focused modules, so I can fix a phase bug without reading 2700 lines.
- As a maintainer, I want Animator/Renderer/TurnController each <800 lines with per-concern helpers, so rendering and turn-validation changes are isolated and reviewable.
- As a maintainer, I want remaining large modules (State, Cards, Adjacency, Market, LifecycleManager) decomposed or explicitly scoped with extracted helpers and updated REFACTOR guards, so the whole Main Street surface meets the threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Line-count threshold met** — Each of the 9 listed files is reduced to <800 lines, or the excess is extracted into new per-concern modules under `example-games/main-street/` and `example-games/main-street/scenes/` with the primary file at <800 lines; `wc -l` per file verified in review and REFACTOR comments removed for compliant modules (remaining guards explicitly justified).
2. **Per-concern splits preserved behavior** — Animator split extracts income-phase choreography, synergy-line, and card-movement helpers; Renderer split extracts grid/market/street rendering helpers; TurnController split extracts market-action validation and turn-advancement orchestration; Engine split extracts phase handlers / action dispatch / scoring helpers; LifecycleManager split extracts checkpoint and CSV/SVG prewarm sub-concerns — each new module has a single responsibility and is imported by its parent with no circular dependencies.
3. **No behavioral regression** — `npm run build` succeeds; targeted Main Street tests pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/` and `--project browser` for affected scenes); full suite green on release verification (`npm test` per quality gates); no changes to public `MainStreetEngine` / `MainStreetState` export contracts except additive extraction.
4. **REFACTOR hygiene and docs** — `grep -r REFACTOR example-games/main-street` confirms no stale guards for completed modules; code comments on new modules document responsibility and import graph; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` or `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` updated only if new patterns affect developer workflow (per doc-update policy).
5. **Documentation and traceability** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Game-local refactor only — not an engine-move; new modules stay under `example-games/main-street/` (no extraction to `src/`).
- Must not break existing save/load, transcript, undo/redo, or tutorial flows; preserve exported types and command signatures.
- Follow AGENTS.md worktree/implement hygiene and ship quality gates (build → test → commit; push to `dev` only).
- Do not duplicate prior closed god-class item CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI (which covered MainStreetScene 3042 etc. — different files); dedup via REFACTOR guard at `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts:2`, `MainStreetAnimator.ts:2`, `MainStreetRenderer.ts:2`, `MainStreetTurnController.ts:2`.

## Existing State

- All 9 files exceed 800 lines today (HEAD counts: Engine 2720, Animator 1948, Renderer 1908, TurnController 1821, Adjacency 1583, State 1582, Cards 1469, Market 1311, LifecycleManager 1111); REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KLQD001TBMH guards injected in 4 files (Engine, Animator, Renderer, TurnController) at line 2 by commit 173b5590.
- Prior god-class CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI covered different scene files and is completed — not a duplicate per AC4.
- Structural causes: Engine mixes DayStart/MarketPhase/InvestmentResolution/IncomePhase/IncidentPhase/EndCheck plus action handlers and scoring; Animator bundles income choreography constants (INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS etc.) with synergy lines and moveGameObject usage; Renderer bundles grid, market, street, HUD tooltip rendering; TurnController bundles canPurchase*/canSell* validation with command orchestration and transcript recording.
- Build and full test suite green at HEAD (04fd1e19 / c3ebc7c3); no active feature branches modifying these modules beyond stashed orphans requiring no merge.

## Desired Change

- Decompose the 9 modules into per-concern helpers targeting <800 lines per file (<500 for scenes where feasible). Preferred grouping for planning: (a) Engine phases + dispatch/scoring, (b) Animator income/synergy/movement, (c) Renderer grid/market/street/HUD, (d) TurnController validation/orchestration/transcript, (e) State/Cards/Adjacency/Market/LifecycleManager sub-helpers (checkpoint, CSV/SVG prewarm, adjacency scoring, card-type helpers). Each group becomes a child work item under this parent with its own tests where behavior is extracted.
- Remove or narrow REFACTOR guards only when the corresponding module passes the threshold; leave justified guards with a comment explaining deferred scope if any file remains above threshold for explicit producer-approved reasons.
- Keep changes surgical and commit per group (build → targeted tests → commit with WIP id).

**Key Files:**
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Primary god module (2720 lines); extract phase handlers (DayStart, MarketPhase, InvestmentResolution, IncomePhase, IncidentPhase, EndCheck), action dispatch, and scoring to new helpers under `example-games/main-street/engine/` or flat sibling files
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — Extract income choreography (INCOME_* constants, phased labels/coin stagger), synergyLineEndpoints usage, and card movement/coin-grid helpers
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Extract grid rendering, market row, street/synergy rendering, and HUD/tooltip composition helpers; consider `MainStreetRenderer/*` or sibling modules
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Extract market validation (canPurchase*/canSell*/canAddToHand), command orchestration (buy*/move*/peek* commands), and transcript/turn-advancement helpers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Extract state shape, phase diagram, and store helpers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Extract business/community/upgrade/event/staff card type helpers and GRID_SIZE/synergyColor groupings
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Extract synergy computation and slot income/phase breakdown helpers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Extract legality/cost/affordability and refund helpers
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — Extract checkpoint persistence and CSV/SVG texture prewarm helpers
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Consumer of the decomposed modules; update imports, preserve scene lifecycle
- `tests/main-street/**/*.test.ts` — Existing unit/browser coverage to preserve; add narrow unit tests for extracted helpers where behavior is newly isolated
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update only if new module layout affects developer workflow per doc-update policy

## Related Work

**Potentially related docs:**
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Dev workflow, testing profiles, doc-update policy
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — Scene-to-API mapping; reference for decomposition patterns
- `docs/dev/refactor-pass-CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ.md` — 16-scope inventory and dedup guardrails for the parent refactor pass
- `AGENTS.md` — Project conventions, worktree/implement hygiene, Stage vs Status lifecycle
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts`, `MainStreetRenderer.ts`, `MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Current large modules to be split (see Existing State)

**Potentially related work items:**
- Parent epic `Refactor pass (CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ)` — in_review; this item is one of 4 filed smell children
- Detection `Hybrid smell detection: example games & tests (CG-0MTHTJZGM003JX8X)` — completed; source of this god-class finding
- Sibling smells `Refactor: split ColorettoScene god class (CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV)` and `Refactor: remove stale @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires disables (CG-0MTP6K42C0010G7F)` / `Refactor: clean stale test disables (CG-0MTP6KUL80008VMR)` — parallel large-file / lint-debt items
- Prior closed `God class: Scene files exceed 1400-1850 lines (CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI)` — Different files (MainStreetScene 3042 etc.), not a duplicate
- Recent refactors `Shared Renderer (CG-0MP12WBH70045LNE)` / `Main Street adapter and migration (CG-0MPOLHCAN0037UUS)` — precedent for extracting rendering helpers

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Scope creep / large diff** — 9 files × ~13.9K lines total tempts a single massive PR; mitigation: split into child work items per module group, ship incrementally, and enforce <800 per file as a hard gate.
- **Risk: Behavioral regression via extraction** — moving phase logic or validation could alter turn flow; mitigation: preserve export contracts, keep changes refactor-only (no feature changes), and require Main Street unit + browser tests before each commit.
- **Risk: Circular imports** — new helper graph could introduce cycles (e.g., Engine ↔ State ↔ Market); mitigation: define acyclic dependency direction (State/Cards/Adjacency/Market are leaves; Engine/TurnController depend on them; Animator/Renderer depend on Cards/Adjacency only).
- **Risk: Test gaps on extracted helpers** — new modules may lack direct coverage; mitigation: add narrow unit tests for extracted pure helpers (adjacency/scoring/validation) as part of each child slice.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Extra opportunities (e.g., promoting shared rendering to `src/ui`) are explicitly out of scope as engine-move; file them as separate `engine-move:*` work items rather than expanding this game-local decompose.
- **Assumption:** 800-line threshold is per file after extraction; producer accepts either flat sibling files or `engine/`/`renderer/` subfolders as long as imports remain relative and barrel-free.
- **Assumption:** No concurrent feature work will heavily mutate these 9 files during decomposition; if it does, rebase per group and re-verify thresholds.

Source: intake design decision — producer can adjust during plan phase; no blocking question emitted.

## Problem statement

`example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` is a single-class game scene of **1808 lines** (threshold 800) that mixes rendering (rows/deck/collections, card faces, take/place animations), input handling (row click zones, mode buttons, ESC toggle), AI turn scheduling, overlay lifecycle (start, color picker, round score, game over), sound wiring, and layout math — all inside `ColorettoScene extends CardGameScene`. The size makes future changes to any one concern risky, review slow, and prevents reuse of helpers across scenes. Decompose into focused helper modules while preserving behaviour byte-for-byte.

## Users

- **Game developers extending Coloretto** — want to add features (new overlays, tweaks to the take/place animations) without wading through 1800 lines.
- **Engine maintainers** — want game-local renderer/animator/input patterns extracted so cross-game duplication can be assessed for eventual engine promotion without polluting src/.
- **Reviewers** — want smaller, concern-separated files with clear ownership when future work touches Coloretto.

### User stories

- As a developer adding a new Coloretto overlay, I can edit a small overlay helper without reading unrelated row/collection rendering and AI scheduling code.
- As a maintainer tracing a rendering bug, I can open a dedicated renderer/animator file and find the affected code without searching a god class.
- As a reviewer, I can verify that a refactor preserves behaviour via existing browser + unit coverage without re-reading the entire scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Renderer extracted:** Row/deck/collections rendering, card-face creation, and collection/row layout math extracted into `ColorettoRenderer` (or equivalent) in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`; `ColorettoScene` delegates all rendering to it (scene keeps orchestration only). No rendering logic remains duplicated in the scene.
2. **Input handler extracted:** Row click handling, mode-button lifecycle, and ESC/mode toggling extracted into a `ColorettoInputHandler` (or equivalent) helper; scene delegates input wiring to it.
3. **AI scheduler extracted or reused:** AI turn sequencing (`runTurn` / delayedCall scheduling, `ai-thinking` phase transitions and the per-player `aiPlayers` wiring) moved into a dedicated AI scheduler helper (or reused from a shared base if one exists — document if reused vs newly extracted). Scene orchestrates via the helper, not inline.
4. **Behaviour preserved:** No user-visible behaviour change — all existing Coloretto tests pass (`tests/coloretto/*.test.ts`, `tests/coloretto/*.browser.test.ts`), and the scene still renders correctly at 2-5 player counts, with take/place animations, reduced-motion behaviour, Last Round card handling, and overlays. `npm run build` succeeds; `npm test -- --project unit` passes at minimum (full suite on release per quality gates).
5. **Size reduced & guard removed or updated:** `ColorettoScene.ts` is reduced below **900 lines** (half the current 1808, comfortably under the 800 + headroom rule) and the `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard comment is removed or replaced with a brief module map comment. New helper files each have a single responsibility and are referenced from the scene.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** (Scenes index / help comments / any layout notes touching the extracted modules.)
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.)

- Prefer game-local helpers in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/` (not engine promotion) — this smell is game-local, per dedup note "Not engine-move."

# Activity log shows coins, reputation and score

The last entry in the activity log should show the end-of-turn totals for **coins**, **reputation**, and **score** on a single line, alongside the existing per-turn net summary row.

## Problem Statement

The activity log already displays a per-turn net summary row (`Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep`), added in CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA. Score is not shown in this summary, so the player must look elsewhere (e.g. HUD) to see their current score at turn end.

## Users and User Stories

- **Player:** "After I click End Turn, I want to see my total coins, reputation, and score at a glance in the activity log — not have to look at the HUD."
- **Player:** "I want to see how much my score changed this turn, so I can tell whether my actions were productive."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The activity log's end-of-turn net summary row is extended to include the score delta. Format: `Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep (score: +/−Z)` — coins, rep, and score all on a single line.
- **AC2:** The score delta is computed as the difference between the current `finalScore` (after EndCheck) and the `finalScore` from the previous turn's end. If the score is unchanged, the entry shows `(score: +0)` or `(score: 0)`.
- **AC3:** The score delta entry appears alongside the existing net row — i.e. the existing `appendTurnNetRow()` function is extended, not replaced.
- **AC4:** The score snapshot survives save/load and replay (carried in `MainStreetState` clone/restore/serialization alongside the existing `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep` fields).
- **AC5:** Tests: unit tests for the extended net-row format pass; full unit suite green.

## Constraints

- Main Street only — no generalisation to other example games at this time.
- Same line as the existing coins/rep net summary (no new log entry).
- Score delta, not running total.

## Existing State

- `appendTurnNetRow(state, turnEnded)` in `MainStreetEngine.ts` (line ~1628) appends `Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep` using `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep` snapshots.
- `finalScore` is updated each EndCheck via `updateScore()` which calls `computeScore()`.
- `dayStartCoins` and `dayStartRep` are stored on `MainStreetState` and survive clone/restore.
- Related completed work: CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA (Per-turn net coin/rep summary row).

## Desired Change

Extend `appendTurnNetRow()` to also track and display the score delta. This requires:

1. Add `dayStartScore` field to `MainStreetState` alongside `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep`.
2. Snapshot the current `finalScore` as `dayStartScore` during `executeDayStart()`.
3. Compute the score delta in `appendTurnNetRow()` and append it to the log line.
4. Wire `dayStartScore` through `MainStreetState` clone/restore and serialization.
5. Update tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `appendTurnNetRow()` (~L1628), `executeDayStart()` (~L917)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `MainStreetState` interface, clone/restore, serialization
- `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` — existing net-row tests (extend)

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA** (Per-turn net coin/rep summary row in activity log) — sibling child of CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ; adds coins+rep net row
- **CG-0MTGX3XSH005VRUI** (All resource-mutating log entries gain effective deltas) — sibling child of CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ; enriches individual action entries with effective deltas
- **CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79** (Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI) — original log implementation

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the score appear on the same line as the existing net row, or as a separate line?" — Answer: Same line.
- Q: "Should the log show the running total score, or the score delta from the previous turn?" — Answer: Score delta.
- Q: "Does this apply to all example games, or Main Street only?" — Answer: Main Street only.

# Intake Brief — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right (CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I)

## Problem Statement
During the Main Street end-of-turn income animation the on-card coin matrix is centred on the card and expands rightwards from the middle, obscuring card art/title and making the accumulation direction unclear. It should be left-anchored on the card face and grow strictly to the right.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants income coins clearly grouped at a consistent left-side location so card information remains legible and the coin count-up reads left→right.
- **Future example-game authors** — reuse `coin-grid` for other tableau games and expect a left-aligned packing convention.

### User Stories
- As a player, when end-of-turn income plays, I see coins accumulate starting at the left edge of each producing business card and filling rightwards, so the growth direction is predictable.
- As a player, with 1–3 coins the first coin sits at the leftmost position, not in the centre of the card.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default coin-grid anchor is on the left side of the business card (not the centre / bottom-right quadrant), with the grid's left edge aligned to the card's left inset and growth proceeding rightwards (row-major, left→right, top→bottom).
- [ ] `packCoins` (and any browser rendering via `createCoinGrid`) is left-aligned: for N icons the first placement is at the left edge (`w/2` from the grid origin) and additional icons extend to the right without re-centring earlier icons. Verified for 1, 3, 5, 10, 15+ icons.
- [ ] Packing behaviour (columns 5 → 10 → 15, shrink then overlap, height-fit scaling) is preserved under the new left-aligned layout; coins remain fully inside `availableWidth`/`availableHeight`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; existing `coin-grid.test.ts` / `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` expectations updated to the left-aligned contract.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing `coin-grid.ts` texture/metrics (`COIN_GRID_SIZE=10`, `COIN_GRID_SPACING=2`, `MIN_COIN_SIZE=4`); do not introduce a second grid component.
- Presentation-only change — no mutation of `SlotPhaseBreakdown` or credited income totals.
- Must work with the current Phaser 4 card containers (centre-origin cards) and `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` lifecycle (`reducedMotion` path retained).
- Keep API compatible or provide a migration for explicit `anchorX`/`anchorY` callers (Animator currently calls `createCoinGrid(s, card)` with defaults).

## Existing State
- `packCoins` computes placements relative to the grid centre (`col*(w+s) - finalGridW/2 + w/2`) and the grid container is anchored at `cardW/4, cardH/4` (bottom-right quadrant centre) with `availableWidth=cardW/2`. A 1-coin case therefore renders near the card centre, not the left edge.
- `createCoinGrid` is consumed only by `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` (with defaults), so callers are centralised.
- Packing and rendering are covered by `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts`; VFX scaling (`iconsForAmount`) is in `coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts`.

## Desired Change
- Move the default grid anchor to the left side of the card (e.g., `availableWidth≈cardW - inset*2` and `anchorX≈ -cardW/2 + inset + availableWidth/2` or an equivalent left-aligned container placement) and make `packCoins` left-aligned so placements start at `w/2` and grow rightwards. Update comments/tests accordingly. Alternative implementations that achieve the same visual (left edge start, rightward growth, no centre bias) are acceptable if they keep the grid inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `packCoins` layout math and `createCoinGrid` default anchor/region; update layout formula and default geometry + doc comments
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — sole `createCoinGrid` consumer; verify default call still correct, no per-slot override needed
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — card container geometry (`slotW/slotH`, `cardContainer` origin) for anchor verification
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — pure packing assertions (centre vs left alignment)
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — Phaser wrapper assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — unaffected but nearby regression surface

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:** `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` header comment (packing policy), `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` (phased income choreography)
- **Potentially related work items:**

# Synergy bonus coins animate along synergy lines to receiving card coin matrix

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature**

## Problem statement

End-turn synergy bonuses are folded into each slot's base income (`currentIncome` / `baseIncome`) so the phased `synergy` income phase never shows coins, and the synergy lines are only a static indicator. Players cannot see *where* synergy income came from — which neighbor gave which bonus and how it lands on the receiving card's coin grid.

## Users

- **Player** — "When my turn ends I want to see synergy coins travel along the glowing synergy lines from the giving card's edge to the receiving card, slowly enough to follow, then land in the receiving card's coin matrix — so the synergy economy reads as a spatial transfer, not a hidden number."
- **Player (reduced motion / replay)** — "I still want the synergy phase to pace and label clearly, but without the line flights; replay/headless should show nothing."

### User stories

- As a player with two adjacent synergistic businesses, when the income phases run I see coins leave the edge of one card, slide along the synergy line at a readable speed, arrive at the edge of the other card and count into its coin grid — in both directions for each pair.
- As a player with a business that has two synergistic neighbors, I see a separate stream along each synergy line into that card's grid, with the sum matching the card's credited synergy bonus.
- As a player with reduced motion enabled, the synergy phase still labels and paces but does not animate line flights; the grid still reflects the credited total at collect.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Phase data separates synergy from base** — `SlotPhaseBreakdown` (and the `applyIncome`/`computeIncome` producers) expose board adjacency synergy as a non-zero `synergyBonus` per slot when applicable, and `baseIncome` no longer includes synergy. The per-slot sum `baseIncome + synergyBonus + repBonus + eventDeltas + upcomingDeltas` still equals the credited total; existing `SlotIncome.total` / transcript totals are unchanged. Covered by unit tests (single pair, multi-neighbor, extended-range `synergyRangeBonus`, zero-synergy, sold-slot, same-type penalty).
2. **Bidirectional line-to-grid coin flights (600 ms)** — During the `synergy` income phase, for every synergy pair (`computeSynergyPairs` / `synergyLineEndpoints` clipped `p1`→`p2` geometry — the shared slot-rect-clipped line), coins animate **in both directions** along the line: from the giver's edge (`p1`) to the receiver's edge (`p2`) and vice-versa, each over **~600 ms** (`INCOME_FLIGHT_MS`) with ~60 ms stagger. Each direction carries the receiver's synergy amount attributable to that neighbor (icons via `iconsForAmount` / `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, clamp ≥1 when amount >0). Arrival increments the receiver's on-card `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid` (incremental `displayed` accumulation, same as base/reputation phases) so grids stay visible until the final collect.
3. **Phased choreography integration** — The synergy phase no longer short-circuits when bonuses exist; it runs between `base` and `reputation` on the existing phase schedule (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS=2200 ms`, phase label "Synergy"), reuses the shared `synergyLineEndpoints` helper (so animated lines never drift from static lines), and preserves the final grid→HUD collection, `incomeCollectionActive` suppression, per-coin `COIN_POP` SFX via `moveGameObject`/`soundManager`, and stagger/overlap handling for multiple pairs (including diagnonal and extended-range pairs).
4. **Accessibility & presentation-only guarantees** — Reduced motion keeps the synergy phase label + pacing but suppresses line flights (no `moveGameObject` tweens), matching other phases; replay/headless (`scene.replayMode`) performs no rendering or audio. The feature is presentation-only: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow, is non-blocking, and failures are swallowed so the turn always advances.
5. **Tests + docs** — New/extended unit tests for phase-data separation and per-neighbor attribution; browser tests for bidirectional `p1→p2` flights (assert start near giver edge, end near receiver grid / no (0,0) regression), multi-neighbor, extended-range, and reduced-motion/replay paths; existing income/coin-grid suites remain green. Docs updated (`docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` or equivalent, inline code comments, scene README/help text as needed).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates state/transcript/turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8); non-blocking, failures swallowed; runs inside the turn-advance window like the existing `animateIncomePhases`.
- Reuse existing helpers: `synergyLineEndpoints` (clipped slot-rect geometry), `CoinGrid`/`createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`packCoins`, `moveGameObject` + `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention, `COIN_POP`), `computeSynergyPairs`, `COINS_PER_ICON` scaling.
- Respect reduced-motion (`SettingsStore` / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption; mute/volume honored via `soundManager`.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop`.
- Must not regress CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ (phased income), CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation), or the `currentIncome`/`currentReputationPerTurn` caching contract.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAdjacency.computeSynergyBonus` / `computeBusinessIncome` use a percentage formula (`effectiveBase * synergyCoinBonus * bonusPerNeighbor * N`) with same-type 0.6 penalty and `synergyRangeBonus` 8-way Chebyshev range; `computeSynergyPairs` enumerates pairs via 8-way `neighbors()`.
- `applyIncome` / `applyCompetitiveIncome` and `computeIncome` fold board adjacency synergy into `card.currentIncome` → `SlotIncome.baseIncome` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown.baseIncome`; `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` is always `0` (hand synergy removed CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN). `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` therefore short-circuits the `synergy` case (`iconsForAmount(roundHalf(synergyBonus)) === 0`).
- `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` is the single source of truth for clipped `p1`→`p2` + `mid` geometry, shared by `MainStreetRenderer.drawSynergyLines()` and `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()`.
- `MainStreetAnimator` phased choreography (`base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`, `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS=2200`, `INCOME_FLIGHT_MS=600`, `INCOME_FLIGHT_STAGGER_MS=60`) creates a `CoinGrid` per producing slot parented to the card container; `countOutCoins`/`flyCoinsIn`/`flyCoinsOut` incrementally `revealInGrid`; `collectIncomeGrids` flies grids to HUD (`coinX = gameW*0.25+70`).
- `coin-grid.ts`: integer economy, `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `packCoins`/`gridColumns` 5→10→15 with shrink/overlap, `createCoinGrid` anchored to card container.

## Desired change

1. **Separate synergy in phase data** — Teach `computeIncome` and `applyIncome` (and competitive variant) to populate `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` from `computeSynergyBonus` (or an equivalent per-slot derivation that stays consistent with `currentIncome` + same-type/staff/upgrade semantics) and reduce `baseIncome` by that amount so the sum is preserved. Decide and document whether `SlotIncome` (preview path) also separates or stays total-preserving for backward compat; the animation consumes `SlotPhaseBreakdown`.
2. **Animate synergy lines as coin conduits** — Replace the synergy phase's midpoint `flyCoinsIn` with a bidirectional line traversal: for each `SynergyPair`, derive the clipped segment `p1` (giver edge) → `p2` (receiver edge) via `synergyLineEndpoints(pair, layout)` for both directions; spawn `iconsForAmount(per-neighbor synergy share)` coin visuals at `p1`, tween each along the segment to `p2` (600 ms, `Quad.easeIn`, 60 ms stagger), then on arrival `revealInGrid` on the receiver's `IncomePhaseSlot` handle (edge→grid is the tween landing → grid pop; no extra teleport needed beyond detaching the flight visual). Per-neighbor share is `effectiveBase * rate * bonusPerNeighbor` (uniform across neighbors) or the proportional split of the slot's `synergyBonus` across its `N` matching neighbors — choose the one that sums to `synergyBonus` and document it.
3. **Keep all other phases/behaviors intact** — phase ordering/labels/timing, `incomeCollectionActive`, SFX, reduced-motion/replay gates, and grid-to-HUD collection remain as today.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — separate per-slot board synergy from base in `computeIncome`/`applyIncome`/`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus`; keep `SlotPhaseBreakdown`/`IncomeResult` contract consistent.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — rework `runIncomePhase('synergy')` + `synergyPhaseSources()` to bidirectional `p1→p2` flights via `synergyLineEndpoints`; add helper to attribute per-neighbor coin counts and to land into `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/synergyLineEndpoints.ts` — shared clipped geometry (no change expected, but its `p1`/`p2` are the flight endpoints).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — reference for static synergy line rendering; no change unless depth/z-ordering needs alignment.
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`iconsForAmount`/`COINS_PER_ICON` (no change expected).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn` wiring if phase data plumbing needs it (likely not).
- `tests/main-street/**` — new/updated unit + browser tests (phase data separation, bidirectional line flights, multi-neighbor, extended range, reduced motion).

## Related work

- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ "Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)" (completed) — phased choreography, `animateIncomePhases`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, `CoinGrid` accumulation, `INCOME_PHASE_*` timing.
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR "Synergy link formation animation" (completed) + CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B "synergyLineEndpoints" — shared clipped synergy geometry.
- CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN "Remove hand synergy — cards in hand must not affect street income" — synergy is board-only; `handSynergyTotal` stays 0.
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 "Integer economy (×100)" — `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `Math.round`, `roundInt`.
- CG-0MRWGPR0G009Z5G6 / CG-0MRWLMNU9000ZFXC / CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4 "Percentage-based synergy formula" — `effectiveBase * rate * bonusPerNeighbor * N`.
- CG-0MSP1HCAS00785MP "8-way synergy adjacency + extended range" — `neighbors()` Chebyshev, `synergyRangeBonus`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Synergy attribution vs displayed total** — Splitting a slot's `synergyBonus` across `N` neighbors must sum exactly to the credited total (rounding with `roundInt`/`COINS_PER_ICON`). Mitigate: derive per-neighbor share from the same formula that produces `synergyBonus` and assert sum preservation in tests.
- **Line-to-grid handoff readability** — Flying along the line then popping into the grid must not look like the coin vanishes at the card edge. Mitigate: flight lands at the card edge (`p2`) then immediately triggers the grid pop (`revealInGrid`) with `COIN_POP` SFX.
- **Multi-pair staggering / visual clutter** — Multiple simultaneous line flights could overlap. Mitigate: per-line stagger (60 ms) and 600 ms duration; keep total synergy phase within the existing gap budget; no extra phase delay.
- **Geometry drift** — Animated lines must match static lines. Mitigate: consume `synergyLineEndpoints` directly; no duplicated math.
- **Scope creep** — This item is synergy phase only; no changes to reputation/event/upcoming phases, no new SFX keys, no deck redesign. Log extras as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map → user): "Direction per pair — both directions or single? If single, how is giver/receiver chosen?" — Answer (user): "yes both directions" — both `p1→p2` and `p2→p1` animate, one stream per card's bonus (i.e., each card in the pair receives coins along the line from its synergistic neighbor). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.
- Q2 (Map → user): "'Relatively slowly' + sequencing — how slow and sequential vs parallel per card with multiple neighbors?" — Answer (user): "lets try 600ms" — keep the existing flight duration (600 ms) as the line traversal speed; lines animate in parallel with stagger (60 ms). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.
- Q3 (Map → user): "Should the income data separate synergy from base, and should arriving coins count onto the coin matrix?" — Answer (user): "yes separate it out, yes arriving coins should count onto the coin grid" — `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` must be populated (board adjacency synergy no longer folded into `baseIncome`), and line arrivals must increment the receiving card's `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid` accumulating until collect. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.

Research summary: Inspected `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (folded synergy in `currentIncome`/`baseIncome`, `computeSynergyBonus` percentage formula, `computeSynergyPairs` 8-way range), `MainStreetAnimator.ts` (phased `animateIncomePhases`/`runIncomePhase` synergy short-circuit, `synergyPhaseSources` midpoint sources, `createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`flyCoinsIn`/`collectIncomeGrids`, timing constants), `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` (clipped `p1`/`p2`/`mid` as single source of truth), and `coin-grid.ts` (`COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `packCoins` 5→10→15). Related work confirmed via `wl search` (synergy/income). Defaults for Q1–Q3 were posed and then confirmed by the user in this session.

## Mini-review record

- **1. Completeness:** Problem, users/stories, 5 measurable ACs + docs+suite ACs, constraints, existing/desired states, key files, related work, and Q&A appendix all present and actionable. No placeholders.
- **2. Capture fidelity:** User Q1–Q3 answers captured verbatim in the Appendix without invention; "relatively slowly" concretized as the requested 600 ms and "edge→edge then to coin matrix" as `p1→p2` via `synergyLineEndpoints` landing into `revealInGrid`.
- **3. Related-work & traceability:** Direct precedents linked (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6, percentage/8-way synergy items); shared helpers (`synergyLineEndpoints`, `CoinGrid`, `COINS_PER_ICON`) explicitly referenced; find-related report to be appended.
- **4. Risks & assumptions:** Added attribution/summing, handoff readability, staggering/clutter, geometry drift, and scope-creep guard with mitigations; assumptions (uniform per-neighbor share, 600 ms parallel stagger) documented.
- **5. Polish & handoff:** Tightened language, copy-pasteable file paths, measurable ACs with verification hooks (unit/browser/docs), and a 1–2 sentence headline in the finish summary.

# Problem statement

The contextual first-bank hint overlay (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) fires during the tutorial when the player ends a turn with spare actions, creating a "dead end" that interrupts tutorial progression and confuses the tutorial state machine. The hint is designed for normal gameplay and should not fire while the tutorial is active.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they expect a linear, guided experience. An unexpected banking hint overlay mid-tutorial interrupts this flow, potentially showing a stale or completed tutorial step after the hint is dismissed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banking hint does not fire during tutorial:** The contextual first-bank hint trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` must check that `tutorialController.isActive` is `false` (i.e., the tutorial is not active). The hint must never fire while the tutorial overlay is showing or a tutorial step is pending.
2. **Banking hint fires in normal gameplay:** The hint continues to fire exactly once when a non-tutorial player ends a turn with `actionsRemaining > 0`, respecting the persistence flag (`hasSeenBankingHint`).
3. **No regression to tutorial flow:** Existing tutorial steps, overlay lifecycle, and step progression remain unchanged. The tutorial still completes through all 26 steps without interruption from the banking hint.
4. **No regression to banking hint:** The hint still triggers correctly in normal gameplay after the tutorial is complete (on the first end-turn with spare actions).
5. **All tests pass:** Existing tutorial unit and browser tests pass; no new failures introduced.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` needs modification (one logical operator change). No new fields, no structural changes.
- **Tutorial-layer only:** The fix is entirely within Main Street's tutorial wiring; no core-engine, card-system, or UI component changes.
- **Existing banking hint implementation preserved:** The `BANKING_HINT_STEP`, `renderBankingHint()`, and `TutorialState` banking hint flag remain unchanged.

## Existing state

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** implemented the contextual first-bank hint with the following trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`:
  ```ts
  if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
      pendingBankingHint = true;
      // persist flag via TutorialState
  }
  ```
- This condition fires when the tutorial is **active** AND the player has spare actions.
- The `renderBankingHint()` method saves the current tutorial step, shows the banking hint overlay, and on dismiss tries to restore the saved step — but if the tutorial step has already advanced (e.g., T6 End Turn completed), the restoration shows a stale step, creating the "dead end."
- The intent from the original brief (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) was that the hint fires **once per save** on the first bankable end-turn — but the implementation does not distinguish between tutorial and normal gameplay contexts.

## Desired change

Change the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` from:
```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```
to:
```ts
if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```

This ensures the banking hint only fires in normal gameplay (after the tutorial is complete), never during the tutorial.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — One-line fix: invert the `tut?.isActive` check in the banking hint trigger (endTurn path, ~line 221).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (completed, merged) — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (parent feature that introduced the contextual first-bank hint).
- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed, merged) — Main Street: action banking (engine-level banking logic).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the producer believes the banking hint should also fire during the tutorial (e.g., as an optional teaching moment), that would require a different design — but the title and description indicate this is clearly unintended.
- **No edge cases:** The banking hint has a one-shot persistence flag; if the hint never fires during the tutorial (which is the fix), it will fire on the player's first non-tutorial end-turn with spare actions — this is the intended behaviour.

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-0.1`; placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−0.1) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```
business,biz-pawnshop,Pawn Shop,300,230,Commerce,...,1,5,0,0,Trades second-hand goods. Does not provide or receive synergy bonuses.,2,...,75,...
```

- `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 230`, `reputationPerTurn = 5`, `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, `tier = 2`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- The Pawn Shop currently **adds** 5 reputation per turn (raw ledger units) and costs 3.00 coins (×100: 300).
- All six tier-2 businesses share `cost 300 / income 230 / rep 5 / ongoingCost 75`; changing only the Pawn Shop is a deliberate divergence.

## Desired change

| Field | Current | Desired |
|---|---|---|
| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-0.1` (reduces reputation 0.1/turn) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |
| `ongoingCost` | `75` | `50` — **assumption**, follows `cost/4` convention; pending confirmation |
| `synergyCoinBonus` / `synergyRepBonus` / `tier` / `baseIncome` | `0` / `0` / `2` / `230` | unchanged |

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ongoing-cost convention (assumption, unconfirmed).** Changing `cost` to 200 implies `ongoingCost = 50` per the documented `max(25, cost/4)` convention; the producer's clarification only covered the purchase cost. Implementer should confirm before touching `ongoingCost`; leaving it at 75 leaves a convention inconsistency (risk: low).
- **Unit conventions.** Costs are ×100 integers; `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw. If the game's ×100 scaling applies to reputation in the current branch, `-0.1` may need to be stored as `-10` — validate against the repo's existing tests before finalising the CSV value (risk: medium; mitigated by AC1's negative-delta assertion).
- **Do not regenerate balances.** Running the balance-cards tool would reassign the Pawn Shop's tier band and overwrite the manual cost; the change is a data-only edit plus tests.
- **Scope-creep guard.** The Pawn Shop's card *description* text could mention its reputation penalty, but that is an extra opportunity — record as a linked work item if desired, not part of this item's scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Pawn Shop row: `reputationPerTurn`, `cost` (and `ongoingCost` per assumption)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — template loading from CSV (read-only; verifies `-0.1` and `200` parse)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome` reputation accrual loop (read-only; confirms negative deltas apply)
- `tests/main-street/…` — new/extended tests (e.g. alongside `business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` / `turn-cash-net.test.ts`) for negative rep/turn and cost 200
- `src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts` — no change expected (verify special case is unaffected)
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — update if the Pawn Shop row description changes

## Related work

- `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02` — "End of game stats" (open; text-overlap match only, no dependency).
- `WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1`, `WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3` — text-overlap matches from the automated report; not related.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — documents the Pawn Shop no-synergy special case.
- Existing Pawn Shop synergy opt-out tests: `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` (all covered by AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Q:** "The description says 'Reduce the cost of the pawn shop to 2' — which field should be changed? `cost` (purchase price, currently 300) → reduce to 2? `ongoingCost` (per-turn operating cost, currently 75) → reduce to 2? Or some other cost field? The reputation change (from +5 to −0.1 per turn) is clear."
   **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "Neither should be reduced to 2. This is from when costs were lower, now it should be 200."
   **Final accepted answer:** the **`cost`** field changes `300 → 200` (×100 scale; 2.00 in game terms). The original "to 2" wording was from an earlier lower-cost economy and is superseded.
   Research summary: inspected `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (pawn shop row), `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (numeric validation), `MainStreetCards.ts` (template loading), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`applyIncome` reputation accrual), `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (ongoing-cost convention `max(25, cost/4)`), and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.
